title: Understanding MAE
text: The Mean Absolute Error (MAE) is a measure of errors between paired observations expressing the same phenomenon. It is calculated as the average of the absolute differences between predicted values and observed values.

title: Effect of Shuffling Data
text: Consider how shuffling the data might affect the calculation of the MAE. Does the order of the data impact the mean absolute error when using a constant model?

hintAnswer: The MAE is calculated as the average of the absolute differences between the constant predicted value and the actual values.
title: Constant Model and MAE
text: When using a constant model, the predicted value is the same for all observations. How does this affect the calculation of the MAE?

title: Impact of Shuffling on MAE
text: Since the MAE is based on the absolute differences between the predicted and actual values, and the predicted value is constant, shuffling the data does not change the MAE.
